s0003.literal: Xiao Mohe; Ren Zhong; Fan Yi; his younger brother Meng; Lu Guangda
s0003.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe; Ren Zhong; Fan Yi; his younger brother Meng; Lu Guangda

s0004.literal: Xiao Mohe, styled Yuanyin, was a native of Lanling.
s0004.idiomatic: Xiao Mohe, styled Yuanyin, came from Lanling.

s0005.literal: His grandfather Jing was a Right General of Liang.
s0005.idiomatic: His grandfather Jing had been a Liang right general.

s0006.literal: His father Liang was Assistant Administrator of Shixing commandery under Liang.
s0006.idiomatic: His father Liang had been assistant administrator of Shixing commandery under Liang.

s0007.literal: Mohe followed his father to the commandery; when he was only a few years old his father died. His uncle by marriage Cai Luyang was then at Nankang, Editorial footnote marker 1. and took him in to raise.
s0007.idiomatic: Mohe went with his father to the commandery; when he was only a few years old his father died. His uncle by marriage Cai Luyang was then at Nankang [1] and took him in to raise.

s0008.literal: When he grew somewhat older he was resolute and brave, with surpassing strength.
s0008.idiomatic: As he grew he proved resolute and brave, with surpassing strength.

s0009.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder went to relieve the capital; Luyang raised troops to resist the Founder. Mohe was then thirteen and rode out alone to fight; in the army none could stand against him.
s0009.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion the Founder marched to relieve the capital. Luyang raised troops to resist him. Mohe was then thirteen and rode out alone to fight; in the army none could stand against him.

s0010.literal: When Luyang was defeated, Mohe went over to Hou Andu, and Andu treated him with great favor; from then on he regularly served under Andu on campaigns.
s0010.idiomatic: When Luyang was defeated, Mohe joined Hou Andu, who treated him with great favor; thereafter he regularly campaigned under Andu.

s0011.literal: When Ren Yue and Xu Sihui led Qi troops in raiding, the Founder sent Andu north to hold off the Qi army at Dragon Tail on Bell Mountain and at the Northern Suburban Altar.
s0011.idiomatic: When Ren Yue and Xu Sihui led Qi troops in raiding, the Founder sent Andu north to hold off the Qi army at Dragon Tail on Bell Mountain and at the Northern Suburban Altar.

s0012.literal: Andu said to Mohe: "You are famed for valor—hearing a thousand times is not equal to seeing once.
s0012.idiomatic: Andu told Mohe, "You are famed for valor—hearing a thousand times is not equal to seeing once.

s0013.literal: " Mohe replied: "Today let the lord see.
s0013.idiomatic: " Mohe replied, "Today let the lord see."

s0014.literal: " When battle came, Andu fell from his horse and was surrounded; Mohe alone on horseback shouted and charged straight through the Qi army. The Qi army broke and scattered, and he was thus able to break free; Andu was saved.
s0014.idiomatic: When battle came, Andu fell from his horse and was surrounded. Mohe alone on horseback shouted and charged straight through the Qi army. The Qi ranks broke and scattered, and he was thus able to break free; Andu was saved.

s0015.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng he was made magistrate of his home county; for merit in pacifying Liu Yi and Ouyang He he was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Bashan.
s0015.idiomatic: At the start of Tiancheng (560) he was made magistrate of his home county; for merit in pacifying Liu Yi and Ouyang He he was repeatedly promoted to administrator of Bashan.

s0016.literal: In the fifth year of Taijian the mass of armies marched north; Mohe followed Area Commander Wu Mingche across the river to attack Qin commandery.
s0016.idiomatic: In Taijian year 5 (573) the armies marched north; Mohe followed area commander Wu Mingche across the river to attack Qin commandery.

s0017.literal: At that time Qi sent the great general Wei Pohu and others leading a host of a hundred thousand to relieve them; their vanguard bore the names "Blue-Head," "Rhino-Horn," and "Great-Strength"—all eight feet tall, with strength beyond the common run, and their spearhead was very sharp.
s0017.idiomatic: Qi then sent the great general Wei Pohu and others with a host of a hundred thousand to relieve them. Their vanguard bore the names Blue-Head, Rhino-Horn, and Great-Strength—all eight feet tall, with strength beyond the common run, and their spearhead was very sharp.

s0018.literal: There were also Western Region barbarians skilled with bow and arrow who never missed the string; the armies especially feared them.
s0018.idiomatic: There were also Western Region men skilled with bow and arrow who never missed the string; the armies especially feared them.

s0019.literal: As they were about to fight, Mingche said to Mohe: "If we kill this barbarian, their army will lose its spirit. You have the fame of Guan and Zhang—you can behead Yan Liang.
s0019.idiomatic: As they were about to fight, Mingche told Mohe, "If we kill this barbarian, their army will lose its spirit. You have the fame of Guan and Zhang—you can behead Yan Liang.

s0020.literal: " Mohe said: "I wish to be shown his appearance; I will take him for you.
s0020.idiomatic: " Mohe said, "Show me his appearance and I will take him for you."

s0021.literal: Mingche then summoned a surrendered man who knew the barbarian and was told the barbarian wore crimson clothes, a birch-bark bow case, and bone nocks at both ends.
s0021.idiomatic: Mingche then summoned a surrendered man who knew the barbarian and was told he wore crimson clothes, a birch-bark bow case, and bone nocks at both ends.

s0022.literal: Mingche sent men to spy and learned the barbarian was in the formation; he then poured wine himself for Mohe to drink.
s0022.idiomatic: Mingche sent men to spy and learned the barbarian was in the formation; he then poured wine himself for Mohe to drink.

s0023.literal: When Mohe had finished drinking he galloped and charged the Qi army; the barbarian stepped forward more than ten paces before the formation, drew his bow but had not yet loosed, when Mohe from afar hurled an iron club that struck him square on the forehead and he fell at once.
s0023.idiomatic: When Mohe had finished drinking he galloped and charged the Qi army. The barbarian stepped forward more than ten paces before the formation and drew his bow but had not yet loosed when Mohe from afar hurled an iron club that struck him square on the forehead and he fell at once.

s0024.literal: More than ten men of the Qi "Great-Strength" unit came out to fight; Mohe cut them down as well, and the Qi army then retreated.
s0024.idiomatic: More than ten men of the Qi Great-Strength unit came out to fight; Mohe cut them down as well, and the Qi army then retreated.

s0025.literal: For his merit he was made Bright-Resolution General and Extraordinary Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Lianping, fief five hundred households.
s0025.idiomatic: For his merit he was made bright-resolution general and extraordinary scattered-cavalry regular attendant, enfeoffed as Baron of Lianping, fief five hundred households.

s0026.literal: Soon his title was advanced to Marquis; he was moved to Grand Master of the Stud, the rest as before.
s0026.idiomatic: Soon his title was advanced to marquis; he was moved to grand master of the stud, the rest as before.

s0027.literal: In the seventh year he again followed Mingche in investing Suyu, routed the Qi general Wang Kande, and for his merit was made Administrator of Jinxi.
s0027.idiomatic: In year 7 he again followed Mingche in investing Suyu, routed the Qi general Wang Kande, and for his merit was made administrator of Jinxi.

s0028.literal: In the ninth year Mingche advanced on Lüliang and fought a great battle with the Qi; Mohe led seven horsemen in first, seized the Qi army's great banner with his own hand, and the Qi host was utterly routed.
s0028.idiomatic: In year 9 Mingche advanced on Lüliang and fought a great battle with Qi. Mohe led seven horsemen in first, seized the Qi army's great banner with his own hand, and the Qi host was utterly routed.

s0029.literal: For his merit he was made Bearer of the Staff, Martial-Resolution General, and Inspector of Qiao.
s0029.idiomatic: For his merit he was made bearer of the staff, martial-resolution general, and inspector of Qiao.

s0030.literal: When Zhou Emperor Wu destroyed Qi, he sent his general Yuwen Xin with troops to contest Lüliang; they fought at Longhui.
s0030.idiomatic: When Zhou Emperor Wu destroyed Qi, he sent his general Yuwen Xin with troops to contest Lüliang; they fought at Longhui.

s0031.literal: At that time Xin had several thousand picked horsemen; Mohe led twelve riders deep into the Zhou army, charging and slashing in every direction, and beheaded and counted heads in great number.
s0031.idiomatic: Xin then had several thousand picked horsemen; Mohe led twelve riders deep into the Zhou army, charging and slashing in every direction, and beheaded and counted heads in great number.

s0032.literal: When Zhou sent the great general Wang Gui to hurry to the scene, he formed a long encirclement and chained the river at Lüliang downstream, cutting off the great army's route of return.
s0032.idiomatic: When Zhou sent the great general Wang Gui to hurry to the scene, he formed a long encirclement and chained the river at Lüliang downstream, cutting off the great army's route of return.

s0033.literal: Mohe said to Mingche: "I hear Wang Gui has only begun to chain the downstream—at both ends he is building forts, and they are not yet finished. If you send us to attack, they surely will not dare resist.
s0033.idiomatic: Mohe told Mingche, "I hear Wang Gui has only begun to chain the downstream—at both ends he is building forts, and they are not yet finished. If you send us to attack, they surely will not dare resist.

s0034.literal: The water route is not yet cut; the enemy's position is not firm. If those forts are built, then we shall be captives.
s0034.idiomatic: The water route is not yet cut; the enemy's position is not firm. If those forts are built, then we shall be captives."

s0035.literal: Mingche then stroked his beard and said:
s0035.idiomatic: Mingche then stroked his beard and said,

s0036.literal: "Seizing banners and storming formations—that is the general's affair;
s0036.idiomatic: "Seizing banners and storming formations—that is the general's affair;

s0037.literal: long calculation and far-reaching design—that is this old man's affair.
s0037.idiomatic: long calculation and far-reaching design—that is this old man's affair."

s0039.literal: Within ten days Zhou troops increased further; Mohe again petitioned Mingche: "Now we cannot obtain battle; advance and retreat have no road. If we slip the army through in a breakout, it is not too great a shame.
s0039.idiomatic: Within ten days Zhou troops increased further. Mohe again petitioned Mingche, "Now we cannot obtain battle; advance and retreat have no road. If we slip the army through in a breakout, it is not too great a shame.

s0040.literal: I ask that you lead the foot soldiers, riding in the litter at an easy pace; Mohe will lead several thousand iron cavalry, driving before and behind, and will surely see you safely reach the capital.
s0040.idiomatic: I ask that you lead the foot soldiers, riding in the litter at an easy pace; I will lead several thousand iron cavalry, driving before and behind, and will surely see you safely reach the capital."

s0041.literal: Mingche said: "Your plan, younger brother, is a fine design.
s0041.idiomatic: Mingche said, "Your plan, younger brother, is a fine design.

s0042.literal: Yet this old man received the sacrificial flesh and held sole command on campaign; I could not win in attack or seize in assault. Now besieged and pressed tight, I have no place to set my shame.
s0042.idiomatic: Yet this old man received the sacrificial flesh and held sole command on campaign; I could not win in attack or seize in assault. Now besieged and pressed tight, I have no place to set my shame.

s0043.literal: Moreover the foot troops are many; as overall commander I must myself remain at their rear and lead them all together.
s0043.idiomatic: Moreover the foot troops are many; as overall commander I must myself remain at their rear and lead them all together.

s0044.literal: Your cavalry, younger brother, must be in front and cannot delay.
s0044.idiomatic: Your cavalry, younger brother, must be in front and cannot delay."

s0045.literal: Mohe thereupon led the cavalry out by night.
s0045.idiomatic: Mohe thereupon led the cavalry out by night.

s0046.literal: Earlier, when the Zhou long encirclement had closed, they also laid ambushes in several tiers on the critical roads; Mohe chose eighty picked riders to charge first, with the rest of the horsemen following behind; by dawn they reached Huainan.
s0046.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Zhou long encirclement had closed, they also laid ambushes in several tiers on the critical roads. Mohe chose eighty picked riders to charge first, with the rest of the horsemen following behind; by dawn they reached Huainan.

s0047.literal: Emperor Xuan issued an edict summoning him back and made him General of the Right Guard.
s0047.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan issued an edict summoning him back and made him general of the right guard.

s0048.literal: In the eleventh year Zhou troops raided Shouyang; Mohe with Fan Yi and the mass of armies went to relieve them, achieved nothing, and returned.
s0048.idiomatic: In year 11 Zhou troops raided Shouyang; Mohe with Fan Yi and the mass of armies went to relieve them, achieved nothing, and returned.

s0049.literal: In the fourteenth year Emperor Xuan died; the Prince of Shixing, Shuling, in the hall drew a blade on Houzhu, wounding but not killing him, and Shuling fled to the Eastern Mansion city.
s0049.idiomatic: In year 14 Emperor Xuan died; Prince Shuling of Shixing drew a blade on Houzhu in the hall, wounding but not killing him, and Shuling fled to the Eastern Mansion city.

s0050.literal: At that time popular sentiment was still unsettled and none moved to punish the traitor; Eastern Palace Attendant Sima Shen reported to Houzhu and galloped to summon Mohe. On entering audience he received the command, then led several hundred horse and foot and first hurried to the Western Gate of the Eastern Mansion to encamp his troops.
s0050.idiomatic: At that time popular sentiment was still unsettled and none moved to punish the traitor. Eastern palace attendant Sima Shen reported to Houzhu and galloped to summon Mohe. On entering audience he received the command, then led several hundred horse and foot and first hurried to the western gate of the Eastern Mansion to encamp his troops.

s0051.literal: Shuling in panic went out from the southern gate; Mohe reined his troops in pursuit and beheaded him.
s0051.idiomatic: Shuling in panic went out from the southern gate; Mohe reined his troops in pursuit and beheaded him.

s0052.literal: For his merit he was made Scattered-Cavalry Regular Attendant and General of Chariots and Cavalry, Editorial footnote marker 2. enfeoffed as Sui
s0052.idiomatic: For his merit he was made scattered-cavalry regular attendant and general of chariots and cavalry [2], enfeoffed as Sui

s0054.literal: [jian] Commandery Duke, Editorial footnote marker 3. fief three thousand households.
s0054.idiomatic: [jian] commandery duke, [3] fief three thousand households.

s0055.literal: The gold and silks Shuling had long amassed amounted to tens of millions; Houzhu gave them all to him.
s0055.idiomatic: The gold and silks Shuling had long amassed amounted to tens of millions; Houzhu gave them all to him.

s0056.literal: Soon he was moved to Palace Attendant and Grand General of Agile Cavalry, Editorial footnote marker 4. with the additional post of Left Grand Master of the Palace.
s0056.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to palace attendant and grand general of agile cavalry [4], with the additional post of left grand master of the palace.

s0057.literal: By old regulation the three dukes' yellow-gate audience halls were furnished with ogre-tail ornaments; Houzhu specially granted Mohe an opened yellow gate, a gate with traveling horses, and ogre-tail ornaments in both audience hall and sleeping hall.
s0057.idiomatic: By old regulation the three dukes' yellow-gate audience halls were furnished with ogre-tail ornaments; Houzhu specially granted Mohe an opened yellow gate, a gate with traveling horses, and ogre-tail ornaments in both audience hall and sleeping hall.

s0058.literal: He also made Mohe's daughter crown prince consort.
s0058.idiomatic: He also made Mohe's daughter crown prince consort.

s0059.literal: It happened that Sui Area Commander He Ruo Bi was stationed at Guangling, watching the lands south of the Yangzi; Houzhu entrusted Mohe with the duty of defense and made him Inspector of South Xuzhou, the rest as before.
s0059.idiomatic: It happened that Sui area commander He Ruo Bi was stationed at Guangling, watching the lands south of the Yangzi; Houzhu entrusted Mohe with the duty of defense and made him inspector of South Xuzhou, the rest as before.

s0060.literal: In the first month of Zhenming year 3, at the New Year's audience, Mohe was summoned back to court; He Ruo Bi seized the opening, crossed the river, and stormed Jingkou. Mohe asked for troops to meet him in battle; Houzhu would not permit it.
s0060.idiomatic: In the first month of Zhenming year 3 (587), at the New Year's audience, Mohe was summoned back to court; He Ruo Bi seized the opening, crossed the river, and stormed Jingkou. Mohe asked for troops to meet him in battle; Houzhu would not permit it.

s0063.literal: Bi advanced on Bell Mountain, Editorial footnote marker 5. Mohe again petitioned: "He Ruo Bi has hung his army deep in enemy country; his sound support is still far, and his ramparts and trenches are not yet firm; men's hearts are fearful. If we send troops in a masked strike, we are sure to win greatly"—Houzhu again would not permit it.
s0063.idiomatic: Bi advanced on Bell Mountain [5], Mohe again petitioned, "He Ruo Bi has hung his army deep in enemy country; his sound support is still far, and his ramparts and trenches are not yet firm; men's hearts are fearful. If we send troops in a masked strike, we are sure to win greatly"—Houzhu again would not permit it.

s0064.literal: When the Sui army came in great force and they were about to go out to battle, Houzhu said to Mohe: "You can settle this for me in one stroke.
s0064.idiomatic: When the Sui army came in great force and they were about to go out to battle, Houzhu told Mohe, "You can settle this for me in one stroke.

s0065.literal: " Mohe said: "In every campaign until now it has been for the state and for myself; in today's affair it is for the state, for myself, and for wife and children.
s0065.idiomatic: " Mohe said, "In every campaign until now it has been for the state and for myself; in today's affair it is for the state, for myself, and for wife and children."

s0066.literal: Houzhu brought out much gold and silk and distributed rewards through the armies, ordering Central Army Commander Lu Guangda to array troops at White Earth Mound on the southern flank of the mass of armies; Pacify-the-East Grand General Ren Zhong was next; Protector of the Army General Fan Yi and Minister of State Affairs Kong Fan were after them; Mohe's army was farthest north. The armies stretched twenty li north and south; advance and retreat at either end, each did not know the other.
s0066.idiomatic: Houzhu brought out much gold and silk and distributed rewards through the armies, ordering central army commander Lu Guangda to array troops at White Earth Mound on the southern flank of the mass of armies; pacify-the-east grand general Ren Zhong was next; protector of the army general Fan Yi and minister of state affairs Kong Fan were after them; Mohe's army was farthest north. The armies stretched twenty li north and south; advance and retreat at either end, each did not know the other.

s0067.literal: He Ruo Bi at first thought there would be no battle and was about to take light horsemen up the mountain to observe the situation; when he saw the mass of armies he galloped down and set his formation.
s0067.idiomatic: He Ruo Bi at first thought there would be no battle and was about to take light horsemen up the mountain to observe the situation; when he saw the mass of armies he galloped down and set his formation.

s0068.literal: Guangda first led his division in pressing close; Bi's army repeatedly fell back, then soon rallied again and further divided troops to strike north and break through the generals. Kong Fan went out to fight; when the armies met he fled. The generals were scattered; the formation was not yet joined when the cavalry broke and ran—halting them would not stop them. Mohe had no place to exert his strength and was seized by the Sui army.
s0068.idiomatic: Guangda first led his division in pressing close; Bi's army repeatedly fell back, then soon rallied again and further divided troops to strike north and break through the generals. Kong Fan went out to fight; when the armies met he fled. The generals were scattered; the formation was not yet joined when the cavalry broke and ran—halting them would not stop them. Mohe had no place to exert his strength and was seized by the Sui army.

s0069.literal: When the capital fell, He Ruo Bi placed Houzhu in the Hall of Virtuous Teaching and set soldiers to guard him. Mohe asked Bi: "Now I am a captive and my life hangs on an instant; I wish to see my former lord once—then to die would be without regret.
s0069.idiomatic: When the capital fell, He Ruo Bi placed Houzhu in the Hall of Virtuous Teaching and set soldiers to guard him. Mohe asked Bi, "Now I am a captive and my life hangs on an instant; I wish to see my former lord once—then to die would be without regret.

s0070.literal: " Bi pitied him and granted it.
s0070.idiomatic: " Bi pitied him and granted it.

s0071.literal: Mohe entered to see Houzhu, prostrated himself and wept aloud, then from the old kitchen took food and presented it; when he took his leave the guards could not raise their eyes to look.
s0071.idiomatic: Mohe entered to see Houzhu, prostrated himself and wept aloud, then from the old kitchen took food and presented it; when he took his leave the guards could not raise their eyes to look.

s0072.literal: That year he entered Sui and was made Founder of a Bureau and Equal in Protocol to the Three Excellencies.
s0072.idiomatic: That year he entered Sui and was made founder of a bureau and equal in protocol to the three excellencies.

s0073.literal: Soon he followed Han Prince Liang to Bingzhou and joined him in rebellion; he was executed by beheading, aged seventy-three.
s0073.idiomatic: Soon he followed Han Prince Liang to Bingzhou and joined him in rebellion; he was executed by beheading, aged seventy-three.

s0074.literal: Mohe was slow of speech and deferential like an elder; yet when facing the enemy on campaign his spirit blazed and wherever he aimed none stood before him.
s0074.idiomatic: Mohe was slow of speech and deferential like an elder; yet when facing the enemy on campaign his spirit blazed and wherever he aimed none stood before him.

s0075.literal: Before he had reached the capping age he followed Hou Andu at Jingkou and loved shooting and hunting; not a day passed without hunting.
s0075.idiomatic: Before he had reached the capping age he followed Hou Andu at Jingkou and loved shooting and hunting; not a day passed without hunting.

s0076.literal: When Andu campaigned east and west, winning in attack and seizing in assault, Mohe's merit was in truth the greater part.
s0076.idiomatic: When Andu campaigned east and west, winning in attack and seizing in assault, Mohe's merit was in truth the greater part.

s0077.literal: His son Shilian in youth was alert and outstanding, daring and brave with his father's manner.
s0077.idiomatic: His son Shilian in youth was alert and outstanding, daring and brave with his father's manner.

s0078.literal: His nature was utmost in filial piety; when Mohe met his violent end and mourning was finished, his longing grew still keener.
s0078.idiomatic: His nature was utmost in filial piety; when Mohe met his violent end and mourning was finished, his longing grew still keener.

s0079.literal: When his father's former guests happened to speak of him, Shilian would answer them, grieving beyond bearing himself, and those who spoke would sigh for him.
s0079.idiomatic: When his father's former guests happened to speak of him, Shilian would answer them, grieving beyond bearing himself, and those who spoke would sigh for him.

s0080.literal: All his life he would not take up knife or axe; men of the time praised him.
s0080.idiomatic: All his life he would not take up knife or axe; men of the time praised him.

s0081.literal: Mohe had a rider Chen Zhishen whose courage and strength surpassed others; for merit in pacifying Shuling he was made Inner Administrator of Baling.
s0081.idiomatic: Mohe had a rider Chen Zhishen whose courage and strength surpassed others; for merit in pacifying Shuling he was made inner administrator of Baling.

s0082.literal: When Mohe was executed, his wife and children had already been registered and confiscated; Zhishen gathered Mohe's corpse and with his own hands prepared the burial—his grief moved those on the road, and gentlemen honored him.
s0082.idiomatic: When Mohe was executed, his wife and children had already been registered and confiscated; Zhishen gathered Mohe's corpse and with his own hands prepared the burial—his grief moved those on the road, and gentlemen honored him.

s0083.literal: Yingchuan's Chen Yu also followed Mohe on campaigns; he was clever and discerning, ranged through the classics and histories, understood wind-omens and military books, could compose literary pieces, was skilled at mounted archery, and rose to advising officer of the prince's establishment.
s0083.idiomatic: Yingchuan's Chen Yu also followed Mohe on campaigns; he was clever and discerning, ranged through the classics and histories, understood wind-omens and military books, could compose literary pieces, was skilled at mounted archery, and rose to advising officer of the prince's establishment.

s0084.literal: Ren Zhong, styled Fengcheng, childhood name Mantu, was a native of Ruyin.
s0084.idiomatic: Ren Zhong, styled Fengcheng, childhood name Mantu, came from Ruyin.

s0085.literal: In youth he was orphaned and lowly and was not regarded by his village and district.
s0085.idiomatic: In youth he was orphaned and lowly and was not regarded by his village and district.

s0086.literal: When grown he was crafty and full of stratagems, with strength surpassing others, especially skilled at mounted archery; the young men of the commandery all attached to him.
s0086.idiomatic: When grown he was crafty and full of stratagems, with strength surpassing others, especially skilled at mounted archery; the young men of the commandery all attached to him.

s0087.literal: Liang's Prince of Poyang Xiao Fan was Inspector of He, heard his name, and brought him in to his close attendants.
s0087.idiomatic: Liang's Prince of Poyang Xiao Fan was inspector of He, heard his name, and brought him in to his close attendants.

s0088.literal: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong led several hundred men of his village and followed Jinxi Administrator Mei Bolong in attacking Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouchun, Editorial footnote marker 6. each battle driving the enemy back.
s0088.idiomatic: In Hou Jing's rebellion Zhong led several hundred men of his village and followed Jinxi administrator Mei Bolong in attacking Jing's general Wang Guixian at Shouchun [6], each battle driving the enemy back.

s0089.literal: It happened that the local man Hu Tong gathered a host to plunder; Fan ordered Zhong and the chief commander Mei Sili to join armies and pacify them.
s0089.idiomatic: It happened that the local man Hu Tong gathered a host to plunder; Fan ordered Zhong and the chief commander Mei Sili to join armies and pacify them.

s0090.literal: He then followed Fan's heir Sili with troops in relief; when the capital fell they turned to garrison Jinxi.
s0090.idiomatic: He then followed Fan's heir Sili with troops in relief; when the capital fell they turned to garrison Jinxi.

s0091.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified he was made Pacify-the-Raider General.
s0091.idiomatic: When Hou Jing was pacified he was made pacify-the-raider general.

s0092.literal: Wang Lin established Xiao Zhuang and appointed Zhong Administrator of Baling.
s0092.idiomatic: Wang Lin established Xiao Zhuang and appointed Zhong administrator of Baling.

s0093.literal: When Lin was defeated and returned to court, Zhong was moved to Bright-Resolution General and Administrator of Anxiang, and still followed Hou Tian in advancing to attack Ba and Xiang.
s0093.idiomatic: When Lin was defeated and returned to court, Zhong was moved to bright-resolution general and administrator of Anxiang, and still followed Hou Tian in advancing to attack Ba and Xiang.

s0094.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Yuning and Inner Administrator of Hengyang.
s0094.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to administrator of Yuning and inner administrator of Hengyang.

s0095.literal: When Hua Jiao raised troops, Zhong took part in his plot.
s0095.idiomatic: When Hua Jiao raised troops, Zhong took part in his plot.

s0096.literal: When Jiao was pacified, Emperor Xuan, because Zhong had earlier sent a secret report to the court, released him without inquiry.
s0096.idiomatic: When Jiao was pacified, Emperor Xuan, because Zhong had earlier sent a secret report to the court, released him without inquiry.

s0097.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he followed Zhang Zhaoda in attacking Ouyang He at Guangzhou and for his merit was made Direct Attendant of the Yellow Gate.
s0097.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taijian he followed Zhang Zhaoda in attacking Ouyang He at Guangzhou and for his merit was made direct attendant of the yellow gate.

s0098.literal: He was moved to Martial-Resolution General and Inner Administrator of Luling; when his term ended he entered court as General of the Right Army.
s0098.idiomatic: He was moved to martial-resolution general and inner administrator of Luling; when his term ended he entered court as general of the right army.

s0099.literal: In the fifth year of the northern campaign of the mass of armies, Zhong led troops on the western route, routed Qi Prince of Liyang Gao Jing'an at Great Xian, pursued north to Dong Pass, and then took its eastern and western cities.
s0099.idiomatic: In year 5 of the northern campaign of the mass of armies, Zhong led troops on the western route, routed Qi Prince of Liyang Gao Jing'an at Great Xian, pursued north to Dong Pass, and then took its eastern and western cities.

s0100.literal: Advancing on Qi and Qiao, Editorial footnote marker 7. he took both.
s0100.idiomatic: Advancing on Qi and Qiao [7], he took both.
